A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prompting and fine-tuning study. All 37 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison; relocated analyses and revised graphical results can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original prompting, execution-feedback, and fine-tuning experiments on CodeContests and TACO, including quantitative results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, training and prompting ablations, behavioral analyses, and oracle-selection results.

M1.justification: The reasoning/instruction/feedback framework, conditional CoT-retry procedure, and RFT objective remain unchanged. Expanded implementation descriptions and prompt terminology do not establish a method change; alternative retry prompts and oracle selection are presented as supplementary analyses.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix B.4 adds HumanEval+, MBPP+, and LiveCodeBench-v4 evaluations beyond v1's CodeContests/TACO coverage. These extend the assessment to other code-generation tasks, with single-turn evaluation on all three additions and multi-turn evaluation on LiveCodeBench-v4.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods are retained. However, v3 Table 8 adds single-turn repeated sampling within the execution-feedback comparison, and Table 10 adds unfinetuned-model and CodeContests supervised-fine-tuning references to the earlier RFT data-mixture comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include transfer testing without CoT at temperature 0.2, controlled retry-prompt comparisons using 200 trajectories at temperature 1.0, and post-hoc per-problem oracle selection in Appendix K. The added SFT comparison evaluates one and two training epochs. These extend the protocols substantially; the retained main experiments keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds retry-wording ablations, expands training controls to SFT, single-turn-only data and removal of CoT responses, and introduces reasoning-token/performance analysis and oracle-selection bounds. Appendix H also adds an intermediate-variable failure example. Prompt-stacking, normalization robustness, and the original MT-versus-ST+MT analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same 10,000 Monte Carlo resamples for estimating pass n@k. v3 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practice; additional generation budgets are experimental sample counts.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, but Figures 2 and 7 revise plotted performance: Figure 2's one-turn pass10@100 changes from approximately 46.6% to 49.6%. New transfer results are mixed, including MBPP+ pass@1 of 63.5% for RFT versus 65.2% for the base model. Tables 9–10 and 12–13 add retry, training-control, and oracle-selection outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal multi-turn setup and Appendix A's pass n@k definition and combinatorial explanation are retained. Appendix K's upper bounds are empirical oracle-selection estimates, not new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about prompting combinations, multi-turn generation, feedback granularity, and internalizing reasoning through RFT. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of SFT degradation through training-data mismatch, rejects a simple token-quantity explanation of prompting success, and discusses transfer outcomes beyond the original benchmarks. It explicitly limits oracle results to estimating improvement potential and expands future-work discussion to reasoning-quality filtering and near-correct training trajectories.

D1.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 substantially expand reproducibility information with chat formatting, dataset counts, LSH parameters, AdamW settings, checkpoint-selection practice, and 170 H100-hours using tensor parallelism and FSDP. The principal RFT learning rate, update count, sequence length, and batch size were already specified in v1; these additions primarily document the existing procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the new benchmarks, pause/thinking-token discussion, prompt tuning, and reasoning critics, including Austin, Liu, Jain's LiveCodeBench, Goyal, Herel and Mikolov, Lester, and Zheng. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices undergo substantial thematic reorganization: v1's mixed additional-results appendix is redistributed into single-turn results, prompting justification, ablations, and behavioral analysis. Fine-tuning documentation is divided into explicit pipeline and training subsections. Main-text editing is lighter, with grammatical corrections, repaired cross-references, and clearer captions and explanations.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5, 6, 9, 12, and 13 and the token/performance scatterplots in Figure 22, while expanding the feedback and training-ablation table structures. It merges v1 Figures 19–20 into one multipanel figure, revises plot axes, repairs the previously malformed behavioral-table caption, and substantially reflows and restyles appendix examples.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens assessment of the RFT contribution through controls missing from v1: supervised fine-tuning, single-turn-only training, and removal of CoT responses. Evaluations beyond CodeContests/TACO broaden the evidence, while detailed training and deduplication documentation improves reproducibility. Transfer results include regressions, and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, but the added controls and documentation resolve important evidential and reproducibility gaps without changing the central claims.
